questions.question: In Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning for a finite hypothesis space $H$, how does the required sample complexity $m$ scale with respect to the error parameter $\epsilon$ and the confidence parameter $\delta$?
options: Logarithmically with $1/\epsilon$ and linearly with $1/\delta$
Linearly with $1/\epsilon$ and logarithmically with $1/\delta$
Quadratically with $1/\epsilon$ and exponentially with $1/\delta$
Linearly with both $1/\epsilon$ and $1/\delta$

questions.question: In Reinforcement Learning, what is a key algorithmic difference between model-free Temporal Difference learning (TD(0)) and Monte Carlo (MC) methods for policy evaluation?
options: TD(0) updates value estimates after every step using bootstrapping, whereas MC methods wait until the end of an episode to update based on the full cumulative return.
MC methods rely on explicit knowledge of state transition probabilities, whereas TD(0) learns directly from sampled experience.
TD(0) produces unbiased value estimates with high variance, whereas MC methods produce biased estimates with lower variance.
MC methods can only be applied to continuing non-episodic tasks, whereas TD(0) requires episodic tasks with defined terminal states.

questions.question: In a soft-margin Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier, what is the effect of setting a very large value for the regularization hyperparameter $C$?
options: It widens the decision margin and increases tolerance for misclassified training points.
It applies strong L2 regularization to the weight vector, forcing all weights closer to zero.
It heavily penalizes slack variables, resulting in a narrower margin and a higher risk of overfitting to the training data.
It transforms the objective into an unconstrained optimization problem equivalent to standard linear regression.

questions.question: In t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE), what primary issue does using a heavy-tailed Student-t distribution (with 1 degree of freedom) in the low-dimensional map space address?
options: Non-convexity of the Kullback-Leibler divergence objective function.
High computational complexity of calculating pairwise high-dimensional probabilities.
Vanishing gradients during the early-exaggeration optimization phase.
The 'crowding problem,' where moderate distances in high dimensions cannot be preserved in low dimensions without collapsing distinct clusters together.

questions.question: When applying Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to a mean-centered dataset $X$ of shape $n \times p$, how are the principal component directions (loadings) related to the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) $X = U \Sigma V^T$?
options: The principal component directions correspond to the right singular vectors (columns of $V$).
The principal component directions correspond to the left singular vectors (columns of $U$).
The principal component directions correspond to the non-zero singular values on the diagonal of $\Sigma$.
The principal component directions correspond to the inverted covariance matrix $U \Sigma^{-1} V^T$.
